claim: Population trajectory 2015-2025: official series vs on-island estimate
on_screen_badge: SRC: WORLD BANK WDI (UN WPP) // ONEI // ALBIZU-CAMPOS ESTIMATE [TIER 1 & 2]
source: World Bank WDI SP.POP.TOTL (UN WPP based, fetched 2026-10-23); ONEI and Juan Carlos Albizu-Campos on-island estimate (brief)
note: The official international series (WDI 2025: 10.94M) shows ~-0.3M since 2018; the -1.1M (11.1M -> <10.0M) is the on-island estimate (brief, not yet checked). The chart shows both.

check.result: ONEI official effective population, as reported from ONEI statements: ~11.11M at end-2021, 10,055,968 at end-2023, 9,748,532 at end-2024 (first year below 10M). The 11.1M -> <10.0M path is the official ONEI series, so -1.1M (-10%) is a conservative reading of it (2021-2024: about -1.36M, -12%). Albizu-Campos (independent) estimates 8.62M for 2023. WDI (UN WPP) still shows 10.94M for 2025. ONEI primary tables not retrieved (site blocks downloads).

claim: National grid availability at the October 2024 collapse
on_screen_badge: SRC: UNE (UNIÓN ELÉCTRICA DE CUBA) OPERATIONAL BULLETINS [TIER 1]
source: UNE (Unión Eléctrica de Cuba) operational bulletins

check.result: Peak demand 3,200 MW confirmed: UNE forecast for 18 Oct 2024 (total disconnection at 11:07 that day). Availability in the same forecast was 1,705 MW (deficit 1,495 MW); reported peak-hour deficits were 1,641 MW (15 Oct) and 1,678 MW (17 Oct). No source found for "under 400 MW available". UNE: 5.87 GW installed, 3.2 GW operational (Argus), consistent with design capacity above 3,000 MW.
